Dhūma-ketu, ‘smoke-bannered,’ is an epithet of mṛtyu, ‘death,’ in the Atharvaveda. Zimmer thinks that a comet is meant, but Whitney considers this extremely improbable. Lanman plausibly suggests that the smoke of the funeral pile is referred to.
Foot notes xix. 9, 10.
Altindisches Leben, 358.
Translation of the Atharvaveda, 914.
Ibid.
Dhūmra in the taittirīya Saṃhitā (i. 8, 21, 1) denotes ‘camel’ according to Bo7htlingk's Dictionary.
